newsitem.title: UK: Wace sells Dutch printing business.
newsitem.headline: Wace sells Dutch printing business.

text.p: British imaging and printing group Wace Group plc said on Tuesday it had conditionally sold its Dutch printing business for 4.2 million stg to State Investment BV.
The owner of the State Investment BV, R Willms, is also the managing director of the Dutch Group, the printing business Wace is selling to State Investment BV.

Wace said the audited consolidated accounts for the year ended December 31, 1996 for the Dutch Group show sales of Dfl 17.57 million (6.67 million stg), profit before taxation of Dfl 1.49 million (0.57 million stg) and net assets of Dfl 0.8 million (0.27 million stg).
The Dutch Group was acquired by Wace in December 1995 as part of its acquisition of Ferry Pickering Group Plc, the carton, printing and specialist packaging company.

"Whilst the directors of Wace recognise that the Dutch Group has generated an acceptable return by way of profits and cash generation, it is now entering a phase...that substantial investment is required for future expansion," Wace said.
